title: Mass-Action Law-Median Principle Algorithm for Biodynamics And Informatics Reveals Equivalence or Analogy to Historical Mathematical and Physical Major Theories
content: The Mass Action Law (MAL) Median Effect equation leads to the Unified General Dynamics Theory and algorithm, which provide interdisciplinary and cross-disciplinary common linkage parameters for computerized, digital, efficient, cost-effective, Econo-green scientific R&D and data science informatics. The MAL- general theory for drug and entity dynamics actions with common parameters (Dm and m); and dose-effect interaction in combinations with a unified combination index (CI), which allows digital simulation of synergism (CI < 1), additive effect (CI =1), and antagonism (CI > 1). The MAL-based input-output sequence, pattern transition, and combinatorics of enzyme reactions led to the discovery of the Second Degree (Squared) Pascal triangle. Surprisingly, the unified theory in life sciences can be linked to centuries-old mathematical problems, such as Riemann’s zeta hypothesis for the critical line and the critical strip, and Euler’s Product of the Prime Function and its properties. The universe has two domains: Life and Non-Life, which manifest the dimensionless relativity ratio with basic codes. For life is a/b = a/(1-a) = (1-b)/b (Floating Ratio), and for Non-Life is a/b = (a + b)/a = 1 + b/a, or  (Golden Ratio). Life and Non-Life can be linked by the two fractional finite and continuous distribution functions of “1”. Life is finite, discrete, and binary, cyclable with the Median-based equilibrium, symmetry, harmony, homeostasis, and optimal conditions; Non-Life is open, fractal, and extendable to infinity, as in mathematics, physics, and AI. Despite numerous mathematical equations having been derived and established since antiquity, the relevance of fundamental principles in biomedical science constitutes only a small fraction of them. Human existence constitutes a tiny fraction of the universe. However, humans evolve and decide the units and methods of measurement in all branches of science. This paper represents a theoretical biologist’s view of the universe, based on 60 years of cumulative exploration and experience, which has encountered significant, surprising findings not available from the traditional, specific-aimed, regulated R&D.
